name: Sicilian Defence: Dragon
summary: 1.e4 c5 and ...g6: Black puts the bishop on g7, where it aims down the long diagonal at White's queenside. Black uses the half-open c-file, the c4 square and the exchange sacrifice on c3; White often castles long and storms the kingside. The course also covers the two common ways White avoids the main lines.

black: Fianchetto the bishop to g7 and keep it: it is the Dragon's best piece.
Use the half-open c-file: ...Rc8, ...Ne5 and ...Nc4, and the exchange sacrifice ...Rxc3 against a king castled long.
Strike the centre with ...d5 when White's pieces are not ready for it.
Against 2.c3 or 3.Bb5+, develop simply and fight for d5.
white: Castle long and storm with h4 and h5; trade the Dragon bishop with Be3, Qd2 and Bh6.
In the Classical with Be2 and O-O, play slowly: f4, Nb3 and pressure on the centre.
Avoid the main lines with 2.c3 or 3.Bb5+ and aim for a quiet centre.

structures.name: Dragon pawns: a7 b7 d6 e7 f7 g6 h7
structures.text: Black has a half-open c-file and a pawn on d6 that guards e5 and c5. White's half-open d-file aims at d6, which is easy to defend. The g6 pawn is the hook that White's h-pawn attacks.

structures.name: Opposite-side castling
structures.text: White on the queenside, Black on the kingside: both sides race with pawns and pieces. Speed matters more than material, and ...Rxc3 is Black's standard way to slow White down.

black: g7 bishop: aims at d4 and b2; never trade it cheaply.
c6 knight: hits d4, then goes to e5 and c4 to block the c4 bishop's diagonal and hit the queen on d2.
c8 rook: on the c-file, ready for ...Rxc3.
Light-squared bishop: d7 or e6 in the main lines.
white: e3 bishop: wants Bh6 to trade the g7 bishop.
d2 queen: lines up with Bh6 and the h-file.
c4 bishop: aims at f7 and the king; Black often trades it with ...Ne5 and ...Nc4.
h-pawn: h4 and h5 to open the h-file.

lines.name: Classical, 6.Be2: a quiet fight
lines.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 d6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. Nc3 g6 6. Be2 Bg7 7. O-O O-O 8. Be3 Nc6 9. Nb3 Be6 10. f4 Qc8

notes.1...c5: The Sicilian: Black fights for d4 from the side and keeps the game unbalanced.
notes.2...d6: Controls e5 and prepares ...Nf6 without allowing e5.
notes.3...cxd4: A wing pawn for a centre pawn: Black will have two centre pawns against one.
notes.4...Nf6: Hits e4 before White can defend it with f3.
notes.5...g6: The Dragon: the bishop goes to g7.
notes.8...Nc6: Develops and hits the d4 knight.
notes.9.Nb3: The knight steps away from trades and from ...Ng4 tricks.
notes.9...Be6: Eyes c4 and the b3 knight; ...d5 may follow.
notes.10.f4: Space on the kingside and the threat f5, hitting the e6 bishop.
notes.10...Qc8: Prepares ...Bg4 to trade White's light-squared bishop and keeps an eye on the c-file.

lines.name: Yugoslav Attack, 9.Bc4: the c-file counterattack
lines.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 d6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. Nc3 g6 6. Be3 Bg7 7. f3 O-O 8. Qd2 Nc6 9. Bc4 Bd7 10. O-O-O Rc8 11. Bb3 Ne5 12. Kb1 Nc4 13. Bxc4 Rxc4

notes.7.f3: Guards e4 and stops ...Ng4 hitting the e3 bishop.
notes.8.Qd2: Prepares Bh6 to trade the Dragon bishop, and long castling.
notes.10...Rc8: The rook takes the half-open file towards White's king.
notes.11.Bb3: Steps out of the way before ...Ne5 hits it.
notes.11...Ne5: Heads for c4 to trade the strong b3 bishop.
notes.13...Rxc4: The rook on c4 hits c3 and d4; ...Rxc3 is in the air.

lines.name: Yugoslav Attack, 9.O-O-O d5: strike in the centre
lines.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 d6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. Nc3 g6 6. Be3 Bg7 7. f3 O-O 8. Qd2 Nc6 9. O-O-O d5 10. exd5 Nxd5 11. Nxc6 bxc6 12. Bd4 Bxd4 13. Qxd4 Qb6

notes.9.O-O-O: White castles first and plans h4 and h5.
notes.9...d5: Black does not wait: a pawn offer that opens lines towards White's king.
notes.11...bxc6: Takes towards the centre and opens the b-file for the rook.
notes.12.Bd4: Offers to trade the Dragon bishop.
notes.13...Qb6: The queen eyes b2 and offers a trade; with queens off, White's attack is gone.

lines.name: Alapin, 2.c3: hit e4 with the knight
lines.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. c3 Nf6 3. e5 Nd5 4. d4 cxd4 5. Nf3 Nc6 6. cxd4 d6 7. Bc4 Nb6 8. Bb5 dxe5 9. Nxe5 Bd7

notes.2.c3: White prepares d4 and avoids the open Sicilian.
notes.2...Nf6: Hits e4 before White can support it with d4 and Nc3.
notes.3.e5: Gains space and kicks the knight.
notes.3...Nd5: A good square: the c3 pawn has taken it from White's knight.
notes.6...d6: Attacks the e5 pawn, the front of White's chain.
notes.7...Nb6: Retreats with tempo on the bishop.
notes.9...Bd7: Develops and challenges the b5 bishop; Black is comfortable.

lines.name: Moscow, 3.Bb5+: trade the bishops
lines.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 d6 3. Bb5+ Bd7 4. Bxd7+ Qxd7 5. O-O Nc6 6. c3 Nf6 7. Re1 e6 8. d4 cxd4 9. cxd4 d5 10. e5 Ne4

notes.3.Bb5+: White develops with check and avoids long theory.
notes.3...Bd7: Blocks with the bishop and offers a trade of light-squared bishops.
notes.6.c3: Prepares d4 to build a centre.
notes.7...e6: With its light-squared bishop gone, Black puts the pawns on light squares; the f8 bishop stays free.
notes.10...Ne4: A strong outpost: no white pawn can chase it.

traps.name: 6...Ng4?: the check that removes the guard
traps.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 d6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. Nc3 g6 6. Be3 Ng4 7. Bb5+ Bd7 8. Qxg4 Bxb5 9. Ndxb5

notes.6.Be3: The Yugoslav move order: Be3 first, f3 next.
notes.6...Ng4: Looks active: it attacks the e3 bishop. But the only guard of g4 is the c8 bishop.

traps.punishment: 7.Bb5+ forces the c8 bishop to block on d7, and then it no longer guards g4: 8.Qxg4 wins the knight. Play 6...Bg7 first; ...Ng4 works only after White's queen has left d1.

traps.name: 9...Nxe4?: the fork trick that fails
traps.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 d6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. Nc3 g6 6. Be3 Bg7 7. f3 O-O 8. Qd2 Nc6 9. Bc4 Nxe4 10. fxe4

notes.9...Nxe4: The mistake: Black hopes for ...Nxe4 and ...d5, forking the knight and the bishop.

traps.punishment: 10.fxe4: the f3 pawn takes back, so there is no knight on e4 to fork. Black is a piece for a pawn down. The fork trick works only when e4 has no pawn guard; here 9...Nxd4 or 9...Bd7 are the moves.
